body: ( update: swapping out apply_torque with state.apply_torque didn't fix the problem of hangs with my users - i presume without exhaustive  proof that there were other similar calls/assignments causing the same behaviour.  I'l downgrade to 4.6 for now. )

(disclaimer: i used chatgpt astra to try make progress on this - it did the work of looking for relevant changelists and suggesting what commands to run to inspect memory.  I asked it to output [instructions](https://gist.github.com/increpare/cce28118ab358d2abb7e89c7c5b9110d) (though I didn't run the test in accelerated mode - step 10) telling me what branches to sync, what build commands to run - I'm not experienced with building godot, but I went through all the steps myself, doing my best to verify every step.  Everything in this comment that is not command output is my words).

Looking into this more, I am able to reproduce the hang on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/630a58a12d2cde110c370626c8a461f415273b59 (on my first try) but not on the commit before, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/1df8f1d38685d8122806378dd2657600c2ed6e5b (I ran the test script three times and didn't get a stall).  This is waay out of my depth, but I think #117268, the pull request associated with this change, might have something to do with the stall.

I also encountered intermittent hangs with threaded physics enabled. In my case, the game froze during normal gameplay without crashing or reporting an error. I didn’t see the p_elem->_root error.

The fix from the closed PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120918 seems to resolve my issue. I also tested your reproduction unchanged on Godot 4.7.2: stock hung after around 40,400 frames, while the patched build completed all 50,000 frames.

I’m not familiar with Godot’s internals, so I can’t judge whether that fix is correct, but wanted to share these results in case they help.
